name: Abstaining From Meat
overview: Scripture acknowledges the provision of meat for human consumption as seen in Genesis 9:3, yet also sets boundaries regarding what is appropriate to eat, as introduced in Leviticus 11 and reiterated in Acts 15:29, which calls believers to abstain from meat offered to idols, blood, and strangled animals. The New Testament further emphasizes sensitivity within the community, encouraging believers to avoid eating meat if it causes a weaker brother to stumble, highlighting the importance of love and unity over personal liberty (Romans 14:1, 21). Thus, abstaining from certain meats is framed not merely as a legalistic requirement but as an expression of faith and care for others in the body of Christ.
